about: Budgets for the layers that live OUTSIDE content/spine/ and are therefore invisible to G-LOAD-BUDGET. Every gate that reads this file PRINTS its measurement on every run — the G-LOAD-BUDGET / G-COMP-REPORT discipline — so drift is visible long before it is a failure. Plan B's gSpineWorld owns the `landforms` and `sheets` sections (G-LANDFORM, G-SHEET-BUDGET); Plan C adds `fabric`, `civil` and `loop` and owns G-WORLD-BUDGET, including this file's existence check.
reportLineGrammar: `world-budget: <family> <n> files, <n> bytes (budget <term>, <term>…)` is the grammar for families measured as FILES ON DISK. EVERY BUDGET TERM CARRIES ITS UNIT, and only the terms a family actually has are printed: `fabric` prints `20 files, 262144 B/file, 4194304 B total`; `civil` prints `600 files, 8192 B/file` and no aggregate term, because it deliberately has none. The bare two-number form this line used to describe printed civil’s PER-FILE cap in the slot a reader had just been taught holds the aggregate, beside a measured aggregate — so at 3 civil files the line read as a 1.8x violation and exited 0, advertising a bound that does not exist. Plan B’s `sheets` line still uses the older bare form. A family whose budget is not files and bytes prints its own units after the same prefix: `landforms` reports `<n> types, <n> instances (budget <lo>-<hi> types, <n> instances)`, because it has no files of its own to count. Any parser of these lines must key on the family name, not on a single fixed shape.
cellKmWhy: PINNED CONSTANT, same discipline as KM_TO_U = 100 and SPINE_CELL_KM = 0.05. 0.5 km over the 400 x 400 km frame is an 800 x 800 grid = 640,000 cells. MEASURED 2026-08-22 by the seam-1 fix pass: 23,680,000 bytes = 22.58 MB resident over the grid's 13 typed arrays, NOT the ~14.7 MB this line and the plan preamble both claimed — that figure counted 9 fields and predates the four pinned-constraint fields (landform, fetchKm, depthM, freshKm). It was an ESTIMATE, never a budget; tools/mapforge/tests/grid.test.mjs now sums every field and pins the total. Changing it changes every landform predicate's meaning.
rosterWhy: content/world/civil/pinned-roster.json is the 41-row authoring TABLE for the pinned records, not a record — the civil per-file cap exists to keep individual records reviewable, which a table legitimately exceeds at 13,230 B measured (Plan D Task 4). Its own cap is the next power of two above that, so the table cannot silently absorb generated geometry either. Deleting this section makes the roster fall back under the 8192 B record cap and red, rather than exempting it silently.
fabricWhy: content/world/fabric/ is Plan C generator output: 13 continent files + world.json, with headroom for the handle ledgers landing beside them. 256 KB per file and 4 MB total is the ceiling that keeps a full fabric load inside the `gates` stage budget below; content/world/civil/ is Plan D authored records — many small files, hence 600 x 8 KB and no aggregate term. Raising either cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
fabricPerFileVsInstanceCeilingWhy: ADJUDICATED 2026-08-23, seam-8 fix pass. maxBytesPerFile and landforms.maxInstances DISAGREE, and this line is the ruling. premisesHandlesWhy DERIVED the handles cap from the instance ceiling — 69,391 x 1.38 = 95,712, next power of two 131,072 — and fabricWhy CHOSE its cap instead. Apply the same method to the fabric and it does not clear: 214,036 x 1.38 = 295,370 > 262,144. MEASURED on the committed seed, which is the sharper form of the same finding: continent-02.json is 214,036 B carrying 360 of the world's 1,740 landform instances (20.7 %, tracking its 18.4 % share of gross land), its instances serialise to 155,729 B (72.8 % of the file, 432.6 B each), so at the sanctioned landforms.maxInstances = 2400 and the same share it holds ~497 instances and the file reaches ~273,300 B — 4.3 % OVER the per-file cap. THE PER-FILE BYTE CAP THEREFORE BINDS FIRST, at about 2,277 world instances, 94.9 % of the instance ceiling. RULING: the byte cap STAYS at the committed maxBytesPerFile 262144 and the instance ceiling stays at the committed landforms.maxInstances 2400. Raising the byte cap to the next power of two would be consistent with premisesHandlesWhy's method and is the wrong trade today: the cap currently binds at 81.65 % occupancy on the largest file, which is a live guard four probes have shown fires, and 524,288 would slacken it to 40.8 % — buying 5 % more instances by discarding a working bound on a file that has doubled. Nobody has asked for those instances. What is NOT acceptable is leaving the disagreement unwritten, which is what this line fixes. WHOEVER NEEDS THE LAST 5 %: raise maxBytesPerFile to 524288 on premisesHandlesWhy's stated method (the next power of two above 295,370), add a line here saying so, and re-measure — do not raise landforms.maxInstances instead, because the binding constraint is one continent's SHARE of the instances, not the world total. scripts/tests/world-gates.test.mjs recomputes this arithmetic from the committed fabric on every run, so if the fabric shrinks until the byte cap stops binding first, or the cap is raised without editing this line, the suite reds rather than leaving a stale ruling behind.
premisesHandlesWhy: content/world/premises/ and content/world/handles/ were under NO byte budget at all until Plan C Task 11 — filed in STATE §10 and §16 and paid here. Both caps are DERIVED, not chosen. PREMISES: one authored file per landmass and content/schemas/world-manifest.schema.json pins landmasses at exactly 13, so a fourteenth premise file is a defect, not growth — maxFiles 13. Measured 2026-08-22: 13 files, 8,241 bytes, largest 813 B; 4096 B/file is 5x that headroom and still catches a premise that has absorbed generated geometry, which is the failure this cap exists for. No aggregate term: 13 x 4096 already bounds it and a redundant second bound is a number to keep in step by hand. HANDLES: one machine-written ledger per landmass, 13 files, 335,033 bytes measured, largest 69,391 B (c02). The ceiling is the INSTANCE ceiling: landforms.maxInstances 2400 against the 1,740 placed today is 1.38x, so 69,391 x 1.38 = 95,712 and 131072 B/file is the next power of two above it; 335,033 x 1.38 = 462,345 and 524288 B total is the next power of two above that. Raising either without raising landforms.maxInstances is a budget failure, not a fix.
loopWhy: The seed-to-map budget, and it is a TABLE for a reason: goal G4 measures per-stage time budgets each with its own fail threshold, NOT one aggregate number, because an aggregate hides which stage regressed and silently drifts to minutes. Six rows, spec 7.6: generate 4/8 s, join + G-MEANING 2/4 s, spine + world gates 15/20 s, SVG sheet build 5/8 s, rasterise (ship-time only) 30/60 s, commit + lock 10/15 s. This file is the single authority for all three consumers — the generator CLI stage report reads it and exits non-zero past the failMs column, the sheet build reads the `sheets` row, and Plan D join budget reads the `join` row. Nobody re-states a number that lives here.

landformsWhy.typeCoverageFloor: 100 of the catalogue's types must actually appear in content/world/fabric/ — a QUOTA, not a target, and the number is real: G-LANDFORM enforces exactly it. It arms only once the fabric holds at least one instance (an empty content/world/fabric/ directory is not a fabric layer), and it WARNS on the development gates while FAILING under --require-complete, which is Gate 2 at promote. An incrementally built fabric therefore degrades and reports; a release with a half-built one does not ship. Raising this number without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
landformsWhy.absentBecause: A lexicon row's absentBecause is a DECLARATION, not a second floor. Declared-and-yet-placed is a hard failure (a stated reason contradicted by a real instance). Unplaced-with-null is a WARNING only: as a failure it demanded all 170 rows be placed or excused, which is a strict superset of typeCoverageFloor and made the number above unreachable — 100 types placed still failed 70 times.

sheetsWhy.maxSheets: The roster, enumerated: 1 atlas + 1 basin + 13 continent (Plan E) + 1 overlay + 1 fabric (Plan C) + 1 synthetic (Plan B) = 18. The design's "<= 16" counted the shipped chart only (1 atlas + 13 continents + 1 basin + 1 overlay) and omitted the review sheets the owner's every-artifact-observable rule requires. Raising this cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.maxSvgBytes: 512 KB, and it STAYS 512 KB: the ceiling above it is not ours to raise. librsvg's libxml2 refuses any single attribute over 10,000,000 bytes (XML_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH, no XML_PARSE_HUGE), measured OK at a 1360 px square frame and FAILING at 1370 px, so a baked underlay's data URI has a hard parser cliff 20x above this budget regardless of what the budget says. Measured 2026-08-20 at the atlas sheet's real 1400x1400 frame with 160 irregular regions: underlay 78,178 B / 0.25 s at 2000 px, whole canary sheet ~248 KB / ~0.79 s — 1.6-2.1x inside this cap. THAT MEASUREMENT IS NOT ROBUST TO COLOUR VARIATION. It rests on the frame holding ~9 distinct colours and on strict tile periodicity, not on geometry: nearly quadrupling the region count to 600 costs only +27%, but a per-region TINT pass drops headroom from 3.3x to 1.33x, and tint plus dither blows 512 KB under every encoding tried, including off-the-shelf zlib -9. Anyone proposing per-region colour variation is proposing to re-decide this number, and must re-measure before doing so. Raising this cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.maxPatternRectAreaRatio: The STRUCTURAL half of the sheet budget, added by Plan B Task 12 because the byte half was not guarding what it looked like it guarded. The basin sheet measured 47,020 B — 11x inside maxSvgBytes — and 11.31 s at rasterWidthPx, 5.7x OVER maxRasterSeconds. Bytes and raster cost are not correlated: librsvg's pattern cost scales with the PIXEL AREA a fill covers, and the sheet drew twelve <rect>s each covering the whole 990x1254 map frame, then clipped every one of them down to a single small zone. 47 KB of text, twelve full-frame tilings. This number is the total area of pattern-filled <rect>s as a multiple of the sheet's own canvas, which is readable straight out of the committed text and therefore checkable by a gate — maxRasterSeconds is not, because a gate must not shell out to rsvg-convert and CI has no librsvg. MEASURED 2026-08-22: defective basin sheet 6.61, fixed basin sheet 0.40, atlas 0.00 (its fills are on <path>s, which cost the shape they actually ink), canary 0.002 (a baked <image> underlay plus 40x24 legend swatches). 1.5 admits a sheet that legitimately pattern-fills its whole canvas and half of it again; it rejects the 6.61 it was calibrated on by 4.4x. Raising this cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.maxPatternRectClipRatio: The DIRECT half of the same rule, added by the F-047 seam-4 fix pass after the two reviewers disagreed about maxPatternRectAreaRatio and both were right. That cap is an AGGREGATE over a whole sheet: verified to fire at 6.61 on the twelve-zone defect, and verified to PASS the same defect at two zones (0.397 + 2 x 0.49 = 1.38 < 1.5). It is a total-cost budget and nothing else measures total cost, so it stays. This number measures the MISTAKE instead — one fill at a time, as a multiple of its OWN clip path's bounding box — so it fires on the FIRST regressed zone rather than waiting for a quorum. MEASURED 2026-08-22 on the committed sheets: worst 1.058 (cluster1 clip-hollowmarch), then 1.053, 1.048, 1.043; the atlas and canary legend swatches carry no clip-path and are exempt, because an unclipped fill is not hiding anything. A single full-frame regression on cluster1’s LARGEST zone scores 24x and on a small one several hundred, so 3 sits 2.8x over the real worst and at least 8x under any regression. Fills whose clip box is under 32 px on a side are skipped: there the emitter’s own 2 px edge slack dominates the ratio and the absolute cost is nil, next to the 1,241,460 px² rects this rule exists for. Raising this cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.maxRasterSeconds: Read by Plan B Task 10's synthetic-sheet raster test, not by a spine gate — a gate must not shell out to rsvg-convert.
sheetsWhy.rasterWidthPx: The width maxRasterSeconds is measured at. A raster budget without its width is not a budget. It is NOT the width anything is committed at — see thumbWidthPx.
sheetsWhy.thumbWidthPx: 512 px, and it is the width of the ONLY raster that is ever committed. `render-sheet.mjs --png` writes at this width; `--png-width 2000` produces the ship raster on demand and that file is never added. The two numbers are separate because they answer different questions: rasterWidthPx is what the 2 s raster budget is measured at, thumbWidthPx is what LFS pays for. 512 px is the smallest width at which F-044's finding still holds — the sheet's sub-pixel ink survives the downscale and the storybook card stays legible; the vector itself vanishes at card scale, which is why a raster is committed at all.
sheetsWhy.maxThumbBytes: 384 KB per committed sheet PNG, enforced by tools/asset-storybook/tests/maps-index.test.mjs (Gate 1 AND CI), not by a spine gate — a gate must not shell out to rsvg-convert. The number is the reason the rule exists: .gitattributes:29 puts game-client/assets/**/*.png in LFS with no cross-version dedup, and the target-density canary shipped at 2,534,694 B before this budget, for a sheet no player ever sees. MEASURED at thumbWidthPx = 512 on 2026-08-21: atlas 50,523 B, cluster1 152,208 B, synthetic canary 312,224 B. The cap is set from the canary, which is deliberately the densest sheet the roster will ever hold (1,740 glyph instances, 340 labels, a full-frame baked underlay) — 1.26x headroom over it, and the pre-rule 2,534,694 B canary is still 6.4x over, so the rule fires on exactly what it was calibrated to catch. The plan predicted "near 100 KB each" and a 262,144 cap; that held for the two real sheets and was refuted by the canary, which the plan was written before. Raising this cap without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.minThumbInkFraction: THE FLOOR THAT DID NOT EXIST. Every rule on a committed thumb bound it from ABOVE — maxThumbBytes caps it, thumbWidthPx pins its width — so a BLANK image passed all of them. Proved at d86f948 by both seam-4 reviewers independently: a 1,899 B blank 512 px PNG substituted for the atlas thumb left the storybook suite 47/0 and check_render_lock, check_asset_manifest and check_content all clean. The one guard that claimed to see it, render-sheet.test.mjs's `size > 10000` on the ship raster, cannot: a blank 2000 px raster measures 14,079-18,074 B depending on the librsvg build, well over its own floor. Compressed size is the wrong variable for the same reason it was the wrong variable for raster cost. This number is the share of PIXELS that differ from the image's own modal colour by more than 8/255 per channel, read by tools/mapforge/lib/png-ink.mjs, which decodes the committed bytes and needs no rendering library — so it runs in CI, which has none. MEASURED 2026-08-22 on the committed thumbs: atlas 0.0545, cluster1 0.2880, canary 0.3037; a blank page of any size scores exactly 0. 0.02 is 2.7x under the sparsest real sheet and infinitely over a blank one. Lowering this floor without adding a line here is a budget failure, not a fix.
sheetsWhy.minThumbInkRowFraction: The second half of the ink floor, because one number cannot see two different ways of being blank. minThumbInkFraction catches the uniform page; this catches the page whose ink is all in one blot — a corner watermark, a legend block with an empty map beside it. It is the share of SCANLINES carrying at least one non-modal pixel. MEASURED 2026-08-22: atlas 0.893, cluster1 0.914, canary 0.947, blank 0. 0.5 says half the height of a map sheet must have something drawn on it, which is 1.8x under the sparsest real sheet.
sheetsWhy.minThumbDistinctColours: The third blank mode: a flat two-colour placeholder that a fraction and a row count both admit. A map sheet is parchment, ink, biome fills, coast echoes and antialiasing — MEASURED 2026-08-22: atlas 1,282 distinct RGB values, cluster1 2,870, canary 1,573. A blank page has exactly 1. 64 is 20x under the sparsest real sheet and rejects anything that is not actually a drawing.

gateRulesThatMustBeGreen.G-ALIAS: a representsNodeId pointer whose target the promotion deleted. Both live pointers (n-site-thornveil -> n-thornveil, n-site-icefield -> n-northern-icefield) run FROM the runtime subtree INTO the chart, so a promotion that amputates the chart breaks them and nothing upstream notices.
gateRulesThatMustBeGreen.G-PARENT: roots.json lists n-atlas but the promoted tree has no subtree under it. A faithful promotion writes that subtree; this fires when it wrote nothing and deleted everything.
gateRulesThatMustBeGreen.G-TOWN-FRAME: content/towns/town-millcross.json joins the spine by spineId. The promotion is the only command that can delete its host node, so a red here is the promotion, never the town plan.

promotionWhy: THE FLOOR THAT DID NOT EXIST. tools/mapforge/promote-world.mjs verified every file a draft's manifest LISTED and refused every file it did not — both guards about PRESENCE — while the harmful direction is ABSENCE, because absence is what causes DELETION. MEASURED 2026-08-23: a draft with an empty content/spine/nodes/ and a manifest that agreed promoted with `errors: []` and printed `promote-world: OK` at exit 0, taking the tree from 44 node files to 7. Only the runtime subtree survived. minTrunkNodes is the composition Plan C Task 10 emits and Plan E's content/spine/trunk-census.json restates: 1 world + 13 continent + 3 ocean + 9 sea + 2 alias-anchor region + 1 town + 1 playroot + 1 playspace + 3 site + 2 fixture = 36. It is a FLOOR, not an equality, so a redraw that adds nodes passes and only a shortfall reds; lowering it is a budget failure, not a fix, and it is the number Plan E must move deliberately. gateRulesThatMustBeGreen is step 5's baseline, and it is a set of RULE IDS rather than a failure COUNT on purpose: the count is a property of the ROOT and not of the promotion — the same faithful promotion of the same draft measured 113 failures in a reviewer's full checkout, 112 in the test fixture's scratch repo (3 of them that root's own missing files, so 109 comparable), so a gate keyed on it reds on the environment. The kinds are invariant: a faithful promotion leaves the carried-canon debt Plan E clears (88 G-NET + 3 G-CANON-LEG plus the region aliases naming towns the redraw deletes) and leaves the spine's own integrity green, because it wrote that spine. The three below are the rules the truncated promotion red and the faithful one did not. It is a POSITIVE list, not an exhaustive taxonomy: add a rule when a promotion defect is shown to red it, with the measurement, and never as a guess. promote-world prints its measurement on every run either way, so a set that has stopped covering anything is visible rather than silent.

supplyLimitedSurveyedRegions.c05/r06: 0 of 58 kit types have a single satisfying cell on this ground, so P10 can place nothing here at all and no instance budget reaches it. Ashen ground with no landform its continent's kit admits: Plan E draws it as walked ground with no marks on it.
supplyLimitedSurveyedRegions.c05/r20: supply-limited: 24 candidate cells, 9 of them placeable under the 2-cell separation, and P10's spill loop already dealt this region everything its ground can carry.
supplyLimitedSurveyedRegions.c07/r06: supply-limited: 31 candidate cells, 11 placeable under the 2-cell separation, already at its bound.
supplyLimitedSurveyedRegions.c08/r06: supply-limited: 30 candidate cells, 11 placeable under the 2-cell separation, already at its bound.
supplyLimitedSurveyedRegions.c08/r08: supply-limited: 27 candidate cells, 10 placeable under the 2-cell separation, already at its bound.

poiWhy: spec §8.4 puts 12-30 points of interest in a SURVEYED region and G-POI enforces both ends. Five of the forty surveyed regions on the committed seed cannot reach twelve, and the seam-7 adjudication (STATE §18) weighed three dispositions and took the third: not fixing P10's supply (it cannot close c05/r06 at all and re-baselines every instance digest), not turning the floor into a warning (a rule that cannot fail is the exact failure the seam existed to prevent), but RECORDING the five. What that section did not reach is that recording them in a TEST leaves the committed root at 5 failures the moment Task 13 lands the fabric, which reds Gate 1 and acceptance criterion 3. So the record lives here, where the gate can read it, and it is a DECLARATION rather than a loosening: a listed region that is short is a WARNING naming its measured count and this reason; an UNLISTED region that is short is still a hard failure; and a listed region that is NOT short is a hard failure too, so an exemption cannot outlive its cause — as is a listed region that is REPORTED rather than surveyed, which is the ONE hole the seam-8 review found in this mechanism and the one flip Plan E's redraw actually performs: the staleness check lived inside the surveyed branch, so a row survived untouched the moment its region stopped being surveyed, and adding a reported region here measured zero failures. The 12-30 band itself is NOT restated here: it is spec §8.4's and it lives once, as a constant in gWorldPoi. The numbers below are review N's, measured against the 2-cell separation. Plan E's redraw is where these five stop being thin, and the third clause is what will make it say so.
